name: Game economy / virtual-currency AML (RMT, gold-farming)
category: Adjacent — financial-crime-shaped abuse inside game economies
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Game-economy integrity and virtual-currency anti-money-laundering: real-money-trading (RMT) detection, gold-farming bot-ring detection, in-game item / currency laundering, and account-trading detection on player-driven economies (MMORPGs, marketplace games, blockchain games, UGC platforms).
domain_fit.one_line_definition: A game-publisher economy / trust-and-safety / fraud engineering team must, within seconds-to-minutes of every in-game trade, currency-grant, market-listing, mailbox transfer, account login or wallet event, score each (account, counterparty, character, address) for gold-farming, RMT, item-laundering and account-takeover signatures so an investigator or auto-action policy can issue a ban-wave, freeze trades, or reverse a transfer before the offending currency exits the platform.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: 1) Score every trade event in real time for RMT — sustained currency-in vs. currency-out imbalance per account, atypical counterparty fan-in (a single 'banker' aggregating from many farmers), and one-way no-equivalent-value trades (a hallmark of gold-handoff), so investigators can ban-wave gold-farmer rings before the buyer logs off. 2) Detect 24/7-grind / gold-farming bot signatures from event-rate features (session-duration percentile per account, idle-vs-active ratio, repetitive route distance over 24h, count of identical loot-yield resource-tile visits per hour), and reuse the same feature substrate that anti-cheat consumes. 3) Detect in-game item-dumping and currency-laundering rings — a freshly seeded mule character receiving high-value items from many sources and immediately listing them at floor on the auction-house / market — using fan-in / fan-out + market-listing-price-z-score features. 4) Detect account-trading / account-takeover-for-resale — a long-dormant account suddenly logging in from a new device/region, immediately liquidating inventory to a single counterparty, with login-geo-distance + dormant-wake + inventory-drain-velocity features. 5) Pre-compute and serve the feature vector that the game's rule engine, ML scorer and case-investigator UI all read at decision time and at appeal-time, so the publisher can answer 'why was this account banned at 14:32:07Z on 2026-02-14?' with a reproducible feature snapshot.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Trade events: trade_completed {ts, account_a, account_b, character_a, character_b, item_id, item_qty, currency_amount, server/shard_id, trade_channel (direct/auction/mail/gift)}. Currency events: currency_grant {ts, account_id, source (quest/drop/sale/mail/admin), amount}, currency_spend {ts, account_id, sink (vendor/auction/mail/recipient), amount}. Market events: market_listing {ts, account_id, item_id, qty, price, channel}, market_purchase {ts, buyer_id, seller_id, item_id, price}. Mail / gift events: mail_sent {ts, sender_id, recipient_id, item_ids[], currency_amount}. Session / behavior events: login {ts, account_id, ip, device_fp, geo, asn}, logout {ts, account_id, session_duration}, location_ping {ts, account_id, character_id, x, y, zone}. Resource events: resource_node_harvest {ts, character_id, node_id, item_id, qty}. Wallet / fiat events (for blockchain games and Roblox-style economies): fiat_purchase {ts, account_id, currency_pkg, usd_amount, payment_method, card_bin/wallet}, cashout / payout {ts, account_id, amount, destination}, on-chain deposit / withdrawal {ts, account_id, address, tx_hash, asset, chain_id}. Account / device events: device_fingerprint_change, kyc_update (for blockchain / 13+ Roblox creator economy), payout_eligibility_change. Common identifiers: account_id, character_id, server/shard_id, device_fingerprint, IP, ASN, geo, transaction_id (for idempotency).
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Counters and sums per account / character / (account,counterparty) pair: count(trades_initiated, 1h/24h/7d/30d), sum(currency_out, window) per account, sum(currency_in, window) per account, ratio(currency_out / currency_in, 24h/7d) (gold-farmer/banker discriminator), count(distinct counterparty_account, 24h/7d), count(one-way trades with item_value_diff > k, 7d). Velocities: trades/hour, currency_in_velocity, currency_out_velocity, market_listings/hour, mail_sent/hour. Session features: session_duration_p50/p99 per account over 7d, idle_active_ratio, count_of_sessions > 12h in 14d (the 24/7-grind signal), count_of_login_days_consecutive (rolling). Repetition / route features: count(distinct resource_node visited, 24h), velocity(unique resource_nodes / hour), distance(traveled, 24h) and distance(geohash/grid-cell, 24h) — the beava distance primitive is a clean fit for repetitive-route gold-farming. Distinct-counterparty cardinality (HLL acceptable for >24h). Fan-in / fan-out: distinct sources of currency to an account in 24h (mule-banker indicator), distinct sinks in 24h. Market-price features per (item_id, server): distribution(listed_price, 24h) via t-digest/KLL, z-score of listing_price vs item_market_p50, count(listings_below_floor*p, 24h) (item-dumping indicator). Geo / ASN features: distinct ips, distinct ASNs, distinct geos per account in 7d, login_geo_distance from last_known (impossible-travel for account-trading). Dormant-wake: time_since_last_login, sum(currency_out, 24h post-wake). For blockchain games: per-wallet on-chain fan-in/fan-out, exposure-category counters joined from Chainalysis/TRM. Mostly multi-window sliding (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d) plus tumbling (calendar-day for daily caps and payout limits).
domain_fit.entity_grain: Multi-grain. Primary keys: (account_id), (character_id), (account_id + counterparty_account) pair, (account_id + server/shard), (item_id + server) for per-market price baselines, (resource_node_id) for grind detection, (device_fingerprint), (ip), (asn). For Roblox / creator economy: (creator_user_id), (developer_product_id), (group_id) for group-funds laundering. For blockchain games: (wallet_address), (token_id), (counterparty_address). The (account_id + counterparty_account) pair is critical for RMT/gold-farming because the strongest signal is repeated low-information one-way transfers along a small set of edges. For peer-group baselines: (game_segment, level_band, region) holds the segment-level distribution.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: Sliding windows dominate at the operational tier: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d for currency velocity, trade fan-in/fan-out, session duration, and price-z-scores. Tumbling calendar-day windows are used for payout caps and daily-limit enforcement (e.g. Roblox creator payout thresholds, blockchain game daily cash-out limits). Session windows are useful for the 'one continuous 16-hour grind session' detector but can be approximated with consecutive-1h-counter chains. Approximate sketches (HLL for distinct-counterparty / distinct-resource-node counts, CMS for heavy-hitter resource-tiles, t-digest / KLL for market-price quantiles) are acceptable for all but hard daily-cap thresholds. Hopping windows (e.g. 30d hopping by 1d) suit peer-group baselines updated nightly.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Mixed by event class. RMT / gold-farming scoring tolerates at-least-once (a double-counted trade biases the velocity feature upward, which is the safe direction for catching farmers). Currency-cap / payout-cap enforcement (Roblox Robux payout, blockchain game daily withdraw cap, in-game cap on daily Auction-House revenue) requires strict idempotency — replaying a trade event must not double-credit currency, double-debit a payout cap, or double-trigger a freeze. Fiat-purchase events (Robux purchases, V-Bucks, blockchain game on-ramps) inherit strict idempotency from payments rails. Beava push-on-event with dedupe-on-(transaction_id / tx_hash) at the producer is the recommended pattern.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Trade-time / market-listing-time inline scoring p99 of 50–300 ms is the practical operational target — the publisher wants to score and (optionally) hold a suspicious trade before the buyer logs off. Roblox publicly positions its risk engine as evaluating 'billions of data points in milliseconds' at point-of-purchase. For non-inline detection (overnight ban-wave, weekly investigator-driven review) the budget widens to seconds-to-minutes. Beava's sub-millisecond TCP / msgpack get / batch_get is well inside any of these budgets; the bottleneck is upstream event ingestion, not feature serving.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Mixed. Velocity / trade-fan-in features must reflect the just-arrived trade (effective freshness ~0 ms, same-event update-and-read) to fire while the offending currency is still in-account. Session-duration / 24-7-grind features tolerate seconds of staleness. Per-item market-price baselines can tolerate minutes to one hour of staleness; peer-group baselines (segment-level distributions of trade counts, currency flows) recompute on an hourly to daily cadence. Dormant-wake / device-trust features are best-effort updated at login. Beava's push-on-event with no broker hop is naturally sub-second-fresh for the hot tier; the slower peer-group tier can be hydrated by a batch job.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Highly skewed by buyer scale. A mid-tier MMO publisher (single live title, 100k–500k concurrent users CCU) typically sees ~5k–30k gameplay events/s and ~hundreds of trade-class events/s. A top-tier MMO publisher with multiple live titles (Blizzard, Square Enix, Bungie, NCSoft, Nexon) is in the tens-of-thousands trade-events/s with millions of gameplay events/s. Roblox operates on a different scale: text-filter peak ~250k requests/s, 40+ data centers, hundreds of millions of MAU, real-time risk scoring on every transaction; total Roblox event volume per day is in the multi-billion range (AWS Gaming reference cites '5B daily events' at Amazon Games as a comparable). Beava's published ~684k EPS on a single Apple-M4 core comfortably covers a mid-tier MMO publisher's full event firehose and a top-tier title's trade-class slice on a single node, with headroom for 30–100 feature reads per decision. A Roblox-scale tenant would exceed single-node capacity and would need horizontal sharding by account_id or server/shard. [uncertain] — per-buyer EPS for game-economy AML specifically is not publicly disclosed; numbers extrapolated from public infra blog posts.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Balanced to read-heavy. Every trade-completed event is one event-write but produces 30–100+ feature reads for rule and ML scoring across (account_a, account_b, item, server). Investigator case-review and appeal flows re-fetch features, adding 5–20x read amplification on the small subset of flagged accounts. Net production ratio is roughly 10–50x reads-per-write, similar to financial AML.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: For a mid-tier MMO: ~5–20M active accounts × ~5–20 KB per-account feature state (multi-window counters, distinct-counterparty HLL, currency-flow sums, dormant-wake, session-duration sketches) plus ~50–200M (account, counterparty) pairs × ~few hundred bytes ≈ ~100–500 GB hot working set. Per-character grain doubles this for games with multi-character accounts (WoW, FFXIV, OSRS). For Roblox / UGC platforms: 100M+ MAU × ~10–30 KB per-user feature state ≈ ~1–3 TB hot working set, plus a long tail of (user, developer_product) and (user, counterparty) pairs. For blockchain games: address-grain cardinality unbounded, comparable to crypto-exchange AML (100M–1B addresses). Beava's in-memory-only model fits a mid-tier MMO on one beefy node; top-tier MMOs and Roblox-scale platforms need sharding or tiered storage. [uncertain] — bytes/entity is an order-of-magnitude planning estimate.
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Mixed. Account cardinality grows slowly (bounded by signup rate). Character cardinality grows faster (multi-character accounts). (Account, counterparty) pair grain is explosive in the long tail but bounded per account (~hundreds of counterparties for a normal player, thousands for a banker). Item / SKU cardinality is small and bounded (hundreds-to-tens-of-thousands per game). Server/shard cardinality is small. Resource-node cardinality is bounded (thousands per game world). Device-fp / IP cardinality is explosive (residential proxies are common in gold-farming). For blockchain games, wallet-address cardinality is essentially unbounded.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Hot velocity features need 7–30d TTL; behavioral baselines need 30–90d; dormant-wake needs 90d+ of last-login per account; account-trading detection benefits from 180d–365d session/device history. Game publishers typically retain raw event logs to cold storage for years (analytics, appeal evidence, regulator-grade for blockchain / Robux payout cases) — beava holds derived features, the cold archive lives in S3/BigQuery/Snowflake/Druid. Roblox Druid OLAP and Spark batch are the canonical cold tier today. Live state lifecycle is materially longer than account-abuse / bot-defence (hours-to-days) but shorter than financial AML (90–365d baselines).
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 30–150 per trade decision is typical: multi-window currency_in/out/ratio, distinct-counterparty, fan-in/fan-out, session-duration, repetitive-route, price-z-score, dormant-wake, device/ip/geo trust, and historical alert count. Investigator review re-fetches a similar or larger vector across linked accounts. batch_get / pipelined-reads are essential.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Crash-safe for trade / market scoring; regulator-grade only for the slice that crosses into payments AML (Roblox creator payouts, blockchain game fiat on/off-ramps subject to FinCEN MSB / FATF VASP rules). For pure in-game economy integrity (Blizzard banning a gold-farmer ring), durability is best-effort to crash-safe — re-deriving features from the upstream event log on a node loss is acceptable because the decision is a ban, not an irreversible money movement. Beava's WAL + periodic snapshot is sufficient; for payout / cashout flows the operator must layer point-in-time / as-of reads and per-read audit if the payout function is in scope.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary-per-region is workable for a mid-tier MMO publisher. Top-tier MMOs typically run regional shards (NA, EU, KR, JP, CN) and would map naturally to one beava per region with no cross-region active-active needed (RMT rings cluster within a region). Roblox-scale needs horizontal sharding (which beava v0 does not natively provide), or partitioning by account_id_hash with a thin router. Sidecar-to-existing-anti-cheat / trust-and-safety platforms (Anybrain, Anti-Cheat Expert, BattlEye, Easy Anti-Cheat, FACEIT Anticheat, Watchdog, in-house) is a realistic adoption path — beava becomes the low-latency feature substrate underneath the publisher's rule engine and case-management UI.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Game-economy / trust-and-safety / fraud engineering teams inside game publishers and platforms: Roblox (explicit Economy Fraud / Risk & Fraud engineering org with active hiring at staff/senior-manager level, public role descriptions cite 'low-latency engines that evaluate billions of data points in milliseconds'); Blizzard (WoW Token / RMT / banwave program); Riot (account-trading and ranked-boosting fraud); Jagex / OSRS (Botwatch, ~4.29M accounts banned in 2025); Square Enix (FFXIV gil-selling enforcement); CCP (EVE Online Team Security, ~70k accounts banned in 2021); Bungie (Destiny RMT and account-recovery); NCSoft / Nexon / Smilegate / NetEase / Tencent (Asian MMO publishers, large gold-farming exposure); Valve (Steam Community Market trade fraud); Mojang/Microsoft (Minecraft Marketplace and Realms); Activision (CoD account-trading). Blockchain games: Sky Mavis (Axie Infinity bot enforcement), Immutable, Yuga Labs (Otherside), GALA Games. Adjacent buyers: gaming anti-cheat / anti-fraud vendors (Anybrain, Anti-Cheat Expert, GGCircuit Watchdog) who could embed beava as a feature substrate. The buyer persona is platform-engineering / trust-and-safety / risk-engineering, not the corporate AML compliance team — except for Roblox creator-payout and blockchain-game cashout flows where AML compliance is directly in scope.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Large and growing. Public scale signals: Roblox 2025 revenue ~$4.9B (+36% YoY), bookings ~$6.8B (+55% YoY), Q4 bookings ~$2.2B — directly enables a dedicated multi-team Risk & Fraud org. CS2 / Counter-Strike skin economy estimated at $4.3–5.2B market cap in 2025 (Bloomberg, late-2025 analyst estimates). RMT-related illicit transactions estimated at over $1.5B annually across MMOs (academic literature). WoW Token effectively monetizes the gold-grey-market at official $20 / token. RuneScape banned 4.29M accounts in 2025, indicating the scale of the bot-farming substrate. EVE Online banned 70k accounts in 2021. The broader anti-cheat software market is estimated at hundreds of millions of USD and growing. Generic AML software TAM ($4–9B globally) is adjacent but mostly addresses financial institutions, not game publishers — game-economy AML is a smaller and more concentrated sub-segment. [uncertain] — no public TAM figure exists specifically for game-economy / virtual-currency AML; figures above are triangulated from public revenue, transaction-volume and ban-volume disclosures.
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: 1) Regulatory: New York AG Letitia James sued Valve in February 2026 over loot boxes / skin gambling in TF2, CS2, DOTA; a related class action followed in March 2026 — both increase pressure on platforms to monitor and demonstrate controls over virtual-currency outflows. 2) FATF 2025 targeted update on virtual assets and VASPs explicitly highlights laundering through in-game purchases and virtual goods. 3) FinCEN's CVC guidance and the MSB exclusion for 'closed-loop ≤ $2,000 prepaid' creates a hard line that platforms with creator-payouts (Roblox, Fortnite Creator Economy 2.0, Unity, blockchain games) must stay inside — driving demand for real-time velocity controls. 4) Roblox's public Hindenburg-style scrutiny on platform safety and reported court filing on ~311 accounts laundering >$1,000 via in-game items (cited March 2023) generates board-level pressure to invest in economy fraud detection. 5) Bot-farming continues to scale: 4.29M OSRS bans in 2025, sustained ban-waves at WoW, FFXIV. 6) Blockchain-game / NFT-game integration with crypto AML rails (FATF Travel Rule R.16, MiCA) pulls gaming AML closer to crypto AML. 7) High false-positive cost: every wrongful ban-wave generates community backlash and refund demands (cf. recent OSRS appeal-process rework), pushing publishers toward more precise feature-driven detection.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: Heavy only on the payout / cashout / fiat-rail slice; light on pure in-game integrity. Where it applies: FinCEN CVC guidance for any platform whose virtual currency is 'convertible' (blockchain games, marketplaces that allow USD cash-out, Roblox creator DevEx); FinCEN MSB registration / BSA program / SAR-filing obligations if the platform crosses the MSB line; FATF Recommendation 15 (VAs/VASPs, 2025 targeted update); FATF Recommendation 16 (Travel Rule); MiCA (EU) for crypto-side; state-level loot-box / skin-gambling rules (NY AG suit Feb 2026, Belgium / Netherlands loot-box bans); GDPR / CCPA / COPPA (Roblox is under-13 heavy, COPPA is the dominant constraint, drives data-minimisation and PII handling); PCI-DSS for fiat-purchase flow. For pure in-game integrity (WoW gold farming, OSRS bot bans), regulatory pressure is weak; the binding constraint is platform-TOS enforceability and community trust.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: 1–2 weeks for a synthetic 'gold-farmer ring' demo: ingest synthetic trade events, compute per-account currency_in/out ratio, distinct-counterparty fan-in, session-duration, repetitive-route distance, and drive a simple rule. 4–8 weeks for a shadow-mode deployment alongside a publisher's existing in-house detector. 3–6 months for a production cutover that ties into the publisher's case-management / ban-workflow tooling. Procurement is publisher-engineering-led and faster than financial AML; open-source / Apache-2.0 is highly attractive because game publishers prefer to own the detection logic (it is a competitive moat against gold-farming arbitrage).

competition.incumbents: Generic streaming + feature-store stacks deployed under game-economy fraud today: Apache Kafka + Apache Flink + Druid is the canonical Roblox stack (public: Spark batch + Flink streaming + Druid OLAP for 'Robux transaction aggregation' and 'real-time trust and safety telemetry'); ClickHouse for in-game-economy metrics ('currency flows, item demand, player wealth distribution'); ksqlDB at Kakao Games (300+ patterns for bonus-abuse, multi-account, ATO, chargeback, affiliate fraud); CockroachDB CDC + Kafka for MMORPG real-time analytics; Redis / Aerospike as low-latency feature caches; Confluent Cloud + Flink ML for in-stream anomaly detection. Generic ML feature stores (Tecton, Feast, Hopsworks, Fennel, Chalk) are present in larger publishers' platforms but not always wired into the economy-fraud loop. Open-source decisioning that overlaps beava's territory: Jube and Marble (both real-time AML+fraud, in-memory state).
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific game-security / anti-fraud vendors: Anybrain (AI anti-cheat + anti-fraud), Anti-Cheat Expert (ACE — 'one-stop mobile game security' explicitly including 'in-game economy risk management'), GGCircuit Watchdog, FACEIT Anticheat, BattlEye, Easy Anti-Cheat (Epic), Vanguard (Riot), VAC (Valve), FiniAC, WeTest. These are mostly process-injection / client-integrity anti-cheat tools, with economy detection as a secondary feature; they do not own the feature-store layer. Most publishers build the economy-fraud loop in-house: Roblox Risk & Fraud org, Jagex Botwatch (account-profiling proprietary system), CCP Team Security, Blizzard's WoW gold-handling enforcement org, Square Enix gil-seller enforcement. Academic / research stack: Detecting Real Money Traders by Trading Network (Fujita et al., AAAI AIIDE), MVAN multi-view attention networks (KDD 2019), PU-Detector PU-learning framework (ACM TKDD 2024 — evaluated on 33.8M transaction logs / 43k players from NetEase MMORPG), 'Unveiling Shadow Markets' scalable anomaly detection (CHI Play 2025, role-based detection with Isolation Forest + XGBoost on Kafka + Spark Streaming, F1 90–92% for banker accounts, 85–88% for gold-farmers). Crypto-side specialists (Chainalysis KYT, TRM Labs, Elliptic) overlap on blockchain-game cashout flows. Quantexa / TigerGraph / Neo4j on the graph / trade-network discovery side. Beava would slot underneath one of these as the feature substrate; it does not replace the trade-graph engine, ban-workflow UI, or the publisher's bespoke detector logic.
competition.beava_differentiator: 1) Single-binary, Apache-2.0, no broker / no ETL — directly attractive to publisher-engineering teams who want to own and self-host their detection moat rather than depend on a third-party SaaS (gold-farming organisations buy SaaS too; sharing a detection vendor leaks signal). 2) The exact set of beava primitives (counters, velocities, distances, distributions, fan-in/fan-out via n_unique, t-digest for price quantiles) precisely matches the published feature catalog from the RMT / gold-farming literature — distance primitive cleanly expresses 'repetitive route' / 'tiny-area grind' detection, fan-in/fan-out maps to banker discriminators, distributions enable per-item price-z-scores. 3) ~684k EPS on a single core covers a mid-tier MMO's entire event firehose with headroom for 30–100 feature reads per decision plus investigator re-fetch. 4) Atomic per-event update-and-read fits the AML-style rule 'the structuring counter must reflect this trade before the rule fires'. 5) HTTP/JSON + framed TCP (JSON/msgpack) — the trade-server / game-server can call beava directly without a Kafka hop, useful for the inline-trade-hold use case where a 2-second broker delay is enough for the gold to exit. 6) Apache-2.0, no open-core, no per-tenant SaaS lock-in — appeals to publisher-engineering teams that resist mixed licences and to anti-cheat vendors who would embed it. 7) WAL + snapshot + refuse-on-network-FS is the right default for any publisher who would otherwise quietly run on NFS and break crash recovery. 8) Aligns with the existing 'Roblox economy fraud / billions-of-data-points-in-milliseconds' narrative, which is exactly beava's positioning.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: 1) No TLS — disqualifying for any production deployment without an in-front mTLS-terminating proxy; many publishers will refuse even with one. 2) No authn / authz / RBAC — publishers running multi-team workflows (Risk & Fraud team, T&S team, Economy team) need per-role tokens. 3) No in-process sharding — caps single-tenant scale at one node, which is a hard limit for Roblox-scale and any top-tier MMO that wants per-shard or per-region partitioning behind one logical service. 4) No native graph / trade-network primitive — the strongest RMT / gold-farming signals (community detection, dense-subgraph trader rings) live in the trade graph, owned by Quantexa / TigerGraph / Neo4j / in-house Spark GraphFrames. Beava can pre-compute per-account fan-in/fan-out counters that feed the graph layer, but it is not the graph engine. 5) No triggers / no webhook on threshold-cross — publishers want 'fire BAN_WAVE_CANDIDATE when currency_out_ratio > k AND distinct_counterparty_fan_in > m' emitted by the feature server; today the rule engine has to poll. 6) In-memory only with long lookback — 90–365 day behavioural baselines (dormant-wake, account-trading) push state size beyond comfortable single-node RAM for large buyers; tiered storage (RAM → SSD) would help. 7) No native point-in-time / as-of reads — publishers need 'what feature values triggered the ban at 14:32:07Z?' for appeal evidence. 8) No case-management UI / no investigator workbench / no ban-workflow — Roblox, Jagex, CCP all run bespoke internal tooling for this. 9) No native sanctions / on-chain risk-label join for blockchain games (Chainalysis / TRM / Elliptic API) — beava doesn't ship a connector. 10) No multi-tenancy for the anti-cheat-vendor embed path. 11) No deterministic replay from WAL with verifiable hashes — important for ban-appeal reproducibility.
competition.integration_surface: Producers: game-server / shard CDC (trade-completed, currency-grant, market-listing events) over HTTP/REST or TCP; mobile / desktop client telemetry for behaviour events; Kafka / Kinesis / Pub-Sub at larger publishers (Roblox Flink-on-Kafka pattern). Wallet / on-chain firehose for blockchain games (custom indexers, QuickNode, Alchemy webhooks). Outbound to: rule engine (Drools, OpenRules, in-house Lua / Python), ML scorer (XGBoost, LightGBM, ONNX, isolation-forest, GNN), case-management / ban-workflow UI (in-house), data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Druid) for analyst review. The natural beava integration is either (a) a thin trade-server-to-beava-TCP sidecar that bypasses Kafka entirely for the latency-sensitive inline path, or (b) a Kafka-to-beava bridge that mirrors the publisher's existing event bus. Most publishers do not run a Tecton/Chalk-class feature store on the economy-fraud path today; the gap beava can fill is 'no-broker no-feature-store' inline scoring.
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. Modern game-economy fraud stacks combine deterministic rules ('ban if 24h-currency-out > N and distinct-counterparty-fan-in > M and session-duration > k hours / day for 7 consecutive days') with ML scorers (XGBoost / isolation forest / GNN on trade graph). The 'Unveiling Shadow Markets' (CHI Play 2025) framework explicitly combines Isolation Forest + XGBoost on a Kafka + Spark Streaming pipeline. PU-Detector (ACM TKDD 2024) uses PU learning on a trading graph. Beava is feature-serving only; the buyer plugs it into both pipelines.

Comparable platforms with named public users and disclosed scale: Roblox (explicit Senior Engineering Manager Risk & Fraud role description disclosing 'low-latency engines that evaluate billions of data points in milliseconds to approve, challenge, or block transactions at the point of purchase' over a 'multi-billion dollar economy'; public Spark + Flink + Druid stack; ~250k requests/s text-filter peak across two core data centers; multi-billion daily events). Jagex (Botwatch + 4.29M OSRS account bans in 2025, 17k+ bans since recent customer-support rework, IP/email chain-bans, behavioural fingerprinting). CCP (~70k EVE Online accounts banned in 2021, Team Security publishes dev blogs on detection methodology; the 2019 blackout banwave is well documented). Blizzard (WoW Token mechanism + explicit Gallywix RMT ban-wave coverage in trade press). Square Enix FFXIV gil-seller enforcement. Sky Mavis (Axie Infinity bot enforcement + bAXS non-transferable reward token introduced specifically to suppress bots). Kakao Games (publicly cites ksqlDB with 300+ patterns for in-game abuse including 'bonus abuse, multiple account usage, account takeover, chargeback fraud, affiliate fraud'). adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: High and continuous, with a tempo between financial AML (weeks-to-months) and account-abuse / bot-defence (seconds-to-minutes). Gold-farming organisations are professional, multi-country operations (cited 12–16 hour shifts in 'gold farms', residential-proxy substrates shared with credential-stuffing operators). RMT marketplaces are publicly indexed (G2G, PlayerAuctions, Eldorado.gg) and operate openly. Adversaries iterate detection-evasion at multi-week cadence — moving traffic between shards, rotating mule accounts, varying session-duration to defeat 24-hour grind detectors. Skin-laundering on Steam Community Market and CS2 third-party markets is adversarial-but-publicly-visible. Net pressure is high; feature drift is real, on a faster timescale than financial AML but slower than payments fraud or anti-cheat aimbot detection.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: 1) Trade-graph community detection / dense-subgraph mining — owned by Quantexa, TigerGraph, Neo4j, in-house Spark GraphFrames; beava feeds aggregate-per-node features but is not the graph engine. 2) Long historical lookback for trade-network back-testing — Spark batch / Snowflake / BigQuery / Druid territory; Druid is the canonical OLAP for Roblox-class platforms. 3) Investigator case-management UI, ban-workflow, appeal-handling — owned by in-house publisher tooling. 4) Client-side anti-cheat (process injection, memory scanning, kernel driver) — Vanguard, Easy Anti-Cheat, BattlEye, ACE, Watchdog. 5) Loot-box gambling-law compliance UI / age-gating / KYC — separate verticals. 6) On-chain wallet labelling for blockchain games — buy from Chainalysis / TRM / Elliptic. 7) System-of-record for accounts, characters, inventory, currency balances — those live in the game's authoritative DB (typically MySQL/Postgres + Redis for hot inventory, or a custom in-house DB). 8) Full event archive for analytics / appeal evidence — that lives in the cold tier (S3, Snowflake, Druid). 9) Trade-graph link-analysis for legal / law-enforcement referral — bespoke investigator tooling, not a feature server.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: To be production-grade for any large game publisher, beava would need (roughly decreasing priority): (1) TLS termination (mTLS preferred) — non-negotiable for any cross-machine deployment; (2) authn/authz with RBAC and per-tenant namespaces — game publishers run multi-team workflows (Risk & Fraud, T&S, Economy, Anti-Cheat) that each need scoped access; (3) triggers / 'fire-on-threshold-cross' webhooks — game-economy fraud is fundamentally event-driven ('emit BAN_CANDIDATE when these features cross') and today the rule engine has to poll; this is the single highest-leverage adjacency feature for this domain; (4) in-process sharding (consistent-hash router, replication, failover) — top-tier MMOs and Roblox-scale need horizontal scale, ideally with the shard key being account_id_hash or server_id; (5) per-feature TTL and tiered storage (RAM → local SSD) — 90–365d behavioural baselines for dormant-wake and account-trading exceed comfortable RAM; (6) hot-standby / synchronous-WAL replication — losing months of session-duration baselines on a node crash is unacceptable; (7) point-in-time / as-of reads — required for ban-appeal reproducibility ('show me the feature values that caused this ban'); (8) idempotency tokens on push (dedupe by transaction_id / trade_id / tx_hash) — required for at-least-once upstream busses without double-counting currency totals; (9) gRPC surface in addition to HTTP/TCP; (10) Kafka source / sink connectors — many publishers already standardise on Kafka and would prefer a managed bridge over a custom sidecar; (11) secondary indexes for investigator queries ('list all accounts with currency_out_ratio>0.95 AND distinct_counterparty>20 in 24h'); (12) per-account 'related accounts' link (e.g. cluster keyed by device_fp / IP / payment_method) to support ban-the-whole-ring policies; (13) on-chain risk-label join (Chainalysis / TRM / Elliptic webhook) for blockchain-game integrations; (14) multi-tenancy for anti-cheat-vendor embedding paths; (15) deterministic replay from WAL with verifiable hashes for ban-appeal evidence; (16) Prometheus + OpenTelemetry exporters for feature-drift monitoring (gold-farmers iterate evasion; the publisher needs to know when a feature stops separating bot-from-human); (17) data-residency controls for regional regulators (Korea PIPA, China PIPL); (18) right-to-erasure surface that does not corrupt aggregate counters — non-trivial design for GDPR / COPPA (Roblox under-13 cohort is COPPA-heavy).
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — strongly. Game-economy fraud is the canonical trigger-action use case: 'when an account's currency_out_velocity crosses k AND distinct_counterparty_fan_in crosses m AND session_duration_24h > j hours for 7 consecutive days, emit BAN_CANDIDATE to the ban-workflow' or 'when a market_listing's price-z-score < -3 AND seller is dormant-wake, hold the listing for investigator review'. Today beava is feature-serving only; the publisher's rule engine has to poll. Adding a trigger / webhook surface (or a 'fire when atomic counter crosses threshold' primitive) is one of the two highest-leverage adds for this domain, alongside TLS+authn.
